name: Two-Stage Sampling with Occupancy Grid and Nonlinear Function
definition: A sampling strategy that combines an Occupancy Grid to skip empty regions (coarse stage) and a nonlinear piecewise exponential function to guide sampling points closer to the object surface within occupied regions (fine stage), reducing training time and sample count while maintaining reconstruction quality.
summary: Two-Stage Sampling with Occupancy Grid and Nonlinear Function reduces training time by skipping empty regions and biasing samples toward surfaces, differing from NeuS and Instant-NGP.
